topics.title: Hear and read familiar greetings
topics.explanation: Learn bonjour and salut as whole words. In salut, the last t is silent. The written u in salut represents a different vowel from the ou in bonjour.
topics.when_to_use: Listen for the difference between u and ou in familiar words. Use the examples as models for these words.
topics.recap: Remember the whole sound of each word. A final letter can be silent in one word and audible in another.

common_mistakes.explanation: The final t of salut is silent in isolation.

exercises.prompt: Which letter is silent at the end of salut?
exercises.explanation: Remember the whole sound of each word. A final letter can be silent in one word and audible in another.

exercises.prompt: Listen, then choose the English meaning.
exercises.instructions: Load and play the French audio before answering.
exercises.explanation: Salut ! means “Hi!”

topics.title: Greetings and polite requests
topics.explanation: Use vous with a person you address formally or with several people. Use tu with one person in a familiar setting. The corresponding request phrases are s’il vous plaît and s’il te plaît.
topics.when_to_use: Start with bonjour in a daytime service interaction. Choose s’il vous plaît when addressing someone politely.
topics.recap: Match the request phrase to the person you address.

common_mistakes.explanation: Use vous when addressing madame politely in this service context.

exercises.prompt: In a polite request to a shop assistant, which phrase fits?
exercises.explanation: Match the request phrase to the person you address.

exercises.prompt: Listen, then choose the English meaning.
exercises.instructions: Load and play the French audio before answering.
exercises.explanation: Bonjour, comment allez-vous ? means “Hello, how are you?”

topics.title: Give and ask for a name
topics.explanation: Use je m’appelle before your first name. Learn Comment vous appelez-vous ? as a complete polite question. In the first expression, me shortens to m’ before appelle.
topics.when_to_use: Introduce yourself when you meet someone. Recognize the full polite question before trying to build new questions.
topics.recap: Use je m’appelle + name. Keep m’ attached to appelle.

common_mistakes.explanation: The fixed expression includes the reflexive pronoun m’.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence introduces someone named Marie?
exercises.explanation: Use je m’appelle + name. Keep m’ attached to appelle.

exercises.prompt: Listen, then choose the English meaning.
exercises.instructions: Load and play the French audio before answering.
exercises.explanation: Je m’appelle Marie. means “My name is Marie.”

exercises.prompt: Introduce yourself as Marie using s’appeler.
exercises.explanation: Je m’appelle Marie. Use m’ before appelle.

topics.title: Recognize numbers zero to ten
topics.explanation: Learn the written number words in small groups. Start with zéro, un, deux and trois, then add quatre, cinq, six, sept, huit, neuf and dix.
topics.when_to_use: Use the number words for simple counts. Practice number spelling first, then listen for the number in a short phrase.
topics.recap: Remember deux for 2, trois for 3 and dix for 10.

common_mistakes.explanation: The written form of 2 ends in x.

exercises.prompt: Which word is the French spelling of 3?
exercises.explanation: Remember deux for 2, trois for 3 and dix for 10.

exercises.prompt: Match each French item with its meaning.
exercises.explanation: Compare each pair with the examples in the lesson.

topics.title: Say how old you are
topics.explanation: French expresses age with avoir + a number + ans. Learn j’ai for your own age and vous avez for someone you address politely.
topics.when_to_use: Use the complete pattern in an introduction. Practice familiar numbers such as dix (ten) and vingt (twenty).
topics.recap: Say j’ai + number + ans. Keep ans even though English uses ‘I am’.

common_mistakes.explanation: French uses avoir to give an age.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says ‘I am twenty years old’?
exercises.explanation: Say j’ai + number + ans. Keep ans even though English uses ‘I am’.

exercises.prompt: J’___ vingt ans.
exercises.explanation: Use ai with j’ in the expression for your age.

topics.title: Ask a simple question
topics.explanation: For a beginner yes-or-no question, keep statement word order and use question intonation in speech. In writing, add a question mark. Learn Quel âge avez-vous ? as a complete polite age question.
topics.when_to_use: Use intonation for short yes-or-no questions. Use quel âge when you need the age itself.
topics.recap: Tu as … ? asks for confirmation. Quel âge avez-vous ? asks for a number.

common_mistakes.explanation: Use quel âge to ask how old someone is.

exercises.prompt: Which polite question asks someone’s age?
exercises.explanation: Tu as … ? asks for confirmation. Quel âge avez-vous ? asks for a number.

exercises.prompt: Build the polite question ‘How old are you?’
exercises.explanation: The correct order is Quel âge avez-vous ?

topics.title: Choose articles with nouns
topics.explanation: Learn each noun with an article. Use un or une for ‘a’ and le or la for ‘the’. Le and la become l’ before a vowel or mute h. The article l’ leaves the noun’s gender implicit.
topics.when_to_use: Use un livre or une table to introduce an object. Use the definite article for an identifiable object.
topics.recap: Learn un livre and une table as pairs. Use l’ami or l’amie before a vowel.

common_mistakes.explanation: Table is feminine, so its indefinite article is une.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase means ‘a table’?
exercises.explanation: Learn un livre and une table as pairs. Use l’ami or l’amie before a vowel.

exercises.prompt: Match each French item with its meaning.
exercises.explanation: Compare each pair with the examples in the lesson.

topics.title: Choose the present form of être
topics.explanation: Être means ‘to be’. Use the subject to choose the present form. Begin with je suis, tu es and il/elle est, then expand to the plural forms and formal vous êtes.
topics.when_to_use: Use être to give an identity, say where someone is, or describe how someone is.
topics.recap: Remember je suis, tu es, il/elle est. Write êtes with its circumflex.

common_mistakes.explanation: Use suis with je. In étudiant, write the initial é.

topics.title: Use avoir for possessions
topics.explanation: Avoir means ‘to have’. Learn its present forms as pairs with the subject. Je becomes j’ before ai. After the verb, name the thing someone has.
topics.when_to_use: Use avoir to describe a possession or ask whether someone has something.
topics.recap: Remember j’ai, tu as and il/elle a. Write a without an accent when it is the verb.

common_mistakes.explanation: Je shortens to j’ before ai.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means ‘She has a bag’?
exercises.explanation: Remember j’ai, tu as and il/elle a. Write a without an accent when it is the verb.

exercises.prompt: Tu ___ une clé.
exercises.explanation: The present form of avoir with tu is as.

topics.title: Make a simple negative sentence
topics.explanation: Place ne before the conjugated verb and pas after it. Before a vowel sound, write n’. With avoir and a negated indefinite object, use de or d’ in these beginner examples.
topics.when_to_use: Use the full ne … pas pattern in standard writing. Start with être, then try n’ai pas de with a possession.
topics.recap: Put ne or n’ before the verb and pas after it. Learn pas de clé as a complete pattern.
examples: I do not have a key.
She does not have a bag.

common_mistakes.incorrect: Je ne ai pas de clé.
common_mistakes.explanation: Ne shortens to n’ before ai.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means ‘I do not have a key’?
exercises.explanation: Put ne or n’ before the verb and pas after it. Learn pas de clé as a complete pattern.

exercises.prompt: Build ‘I do not have a key.’
exercises.explanation: The correct order is Je n’ai pas de clé.

topics.title: Talk about your family
topics.explanation: Use mon with a masculine singular noun, ma with a feminine singular noun and mes with a plural noun. Use mon before a feminine noun that begins with a vowel sound, as in mon amie.
topics.when_to_use: Use these forms to name people or things you associate with yourself.
topics.recap: Choose mon, ma or mes by looking at the noun that follows.

common_mistakes.explanation: Parents is plural. Mes works for both genders in the plural.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase means ‘my parents’?
exercises.explanation: Choose mon, ma or mes by looking at the noun that follows.

exercises.prompt: Voici ___ mère.
exercises.explanation: Mère is feminine singular and starts with a consonant sound.

topics.title: Use regular present forms
topics.explanation: For a regular verb such as parler, remove -er and attach the ending for the subject. Learn irregular verbs such as aller and faire in separate groups.
topics.when_to_use: Use these forms to describe familiar actions and places. Start with parler and habiter.
topics.recap: Remember je parle, tu parles and nous parlons. Write j’habite before the mute h.

common_mistakes.explanation: The regular ending with nous is -ons.

exercises.prompt: Which form completes ‘Nous ___ français’?
exercises.explanation: Remember je parle, tu parles and nous parlons. Write j’habite before the mute h.

exercises.prompt: Listen, then choose the English meaning.
exercises.instructions: Load and play the French audio before answering.
exercises.explanation: J’habite à Paris. means “I live in Paris.”

topics.title: Order something politely
topics.explanation: Learn je voudrais as a complete phrase meaning ‘I would like’. Put the item after it. Add s’il vous plaît in a service interaction.
topics.when_to_use: Use the phrase when ordering at a café or asking for something in a shop.
topics.recap: Use je voudrais + item + s’il vous plaît. For a price, recognize combien coûte … ?
examples: Je voudrais un café, s’il vous plaît.
I would like a coffee, please.

common_mistakes.explanation: Write the final s in voudrais for this polite request.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase asks politely for a croissant?
exercises.explanation: Use je voudrais + item + s’il vous plaît. For a price, recognize combien coûte … ?

exercises.prompt: Listen, then choose the English meaning.
exercises.instructions: Load and play the French audio before answering.
exercises.explanation: Je voudrais un café, s’il vous plaît. means “I would like a coffee, please.”
